From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>

Subject: MAP endgame: credentialing & peering acceptance plan

Hi Elaine,

Thanks again for the productive MAP sync earlier. As we move into the final acceptance window for the POC, I wanted to capture the immediate checklist items we need to close the environment so both teams can run production-like workloads:

1) API credentials: Redwood will issue a scoped API key for your trial account (read/generate only). We recommend a 30-day TTL for trial keys and will provision a service account if you prefer longer-lived credentials. Please confirm: who on your side will be the org admin to accept / rotate keys?

2) Org setup: we need the account alias you'd like us to create (suggested: medarc-trial) and a primary billing contact. We can create the org and invite up to 3 members for initial tests.

3) IP allowlist: please share the CIDR blocks that must be allowed from your end. For minimal latency tests we ask for outbound allowlist to include Redwood egress: 34.120.0.0/16 and 35.190.0.0/16 (we can narrow per-region upon request).

4) VPC peering: if you want private peering, we'll need your VPC name, project/account id, and a proposed peering window. Our infra team prefers a five-business-day window to validate routes and test failover.

Attached: MAP-final-v2.xlsx (updated milestones), redwood-network-template.md and a short VPC peering checklist.

Proposed timeline:
- Wed May 2: exchange org & network details
- Fri May 5: API key issued & org invite sent
- Tue May 9: VPC peering established and smoke tests

If any of these dates are tight for MedArc, propose alternatives and we'll adjust.

Thanks — I copied Neha (security/compliance) and Rachel (onboarding) to help coordinate.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

+1 415-555-0142

Adding tech details for the peering and API issuance so MedArc's cloud team has everything in one place.

API credentials:
- We'll provision a scoped API key tied to service account redwood-medarc-trial (role: inference-client). Key TTL: 30 days by default.
- Rotation: we can rotate via the Console or API; recommend a single rotation during mid-POC (day 15).

IP allowlist notes:
- Redwood egress ranges for US (subject to change): 34.120.0.0/16, 35.190.0.0/16. If MedArc wants per-instance egress IPs we can provide a narrower /24 on request but that requires an additional NAT setup.

GCP VPC peering checklist (summary):
1) Exchange project id & VPC name (received above).
2) Confirm non-overlapping CIDR ranges — we need to avoid 10.0.0.0/16 collisions. If overlap exists, we will fall back to secure ingress over TLS to the public API with strict IP allowlist.
3) Create peering under medarc-prod-vpc-usw1 -> redwood-infra-vpc-usw1 (we will initiate our side after you accept).
4) Configure routes and test subnets: suggest 10.40.0.0/20 for the test subnet on Redwood side.
5) Timeboxed validation: 48 hours of smoke tests + token-latency sampling.

We expect to run an end-to-end inference smoke test that exercises KV cache hits and batching; that test will take ~2 hours once peering and API keys are in place. I'll attach the peering commands and a minimal test plan.

Attachments: vpc-peering-commands.txt (stub), poc-smoke-test-plan.md (stub).
